title: Looking west down Orser Street towards Keith & Plummer Store
description: This photograph of Hartland, taken between 1891 and 1895, looks north along the street. The first building on the left was the C. Humphrey Taylor Store, followed by John Barnett's residence. The third building was the Keith & Plummer General Store, established before 1897, and the fourth was John T. G. Carr's first store, opened in 1884. The eighth building in the row was the Burtt Store and Hall, while the ninth housed the Matheson Blacksmith Shop and Hall. On the right side, the large home belonged to John T. G. Carr, which was later replaced by a three-storey brick building and became the Day & Ross Headquarters. The fenced area eventually became the site of the C. Humphrey Taylor Block, and the partially visible home on the right belonged to George Boyer. Built in 1860, Boyer’s home was the Village of Hartland’s first post office and drug store.
